links.comparator_used: Direct native-language processing (native-language inference) by the same LLMs/VLMs; English chain-of-thought was a third paradigm
links.outcome: Task performance across four clinical tasks in five languages
links.effect: Back-translation pivot consistently restored performance; no pooled numbers are given in the abstract. In the prospective study, correction burden was 59·0% for Thai-pivot, 50·7% for English-pivot and 51·0% for Chinese-direct.
links.tradeoff: In the prospective study, 98·7% of records still required physician edits (overall modification score 53·6%). Thai-pivot correction burden (59·0%) exceeded English-pivot (50·7%, p=0·003) and Chinese-direct (51·0%, p=0·004).

links.comparator_used: No reliability scoring beyond the model's output (perplexity-based confidence evaluated as the reliability signal for flagging errors)
links.outcome: Ability of perplexity-based confidence to flag erroneous outputs
links.effect: AUROC 0·41–0·66 for flagging errors with perplexity-based confidence; the token-level toolkit localised instability to mid-chain stages (40–70% of the normalised trajectory).
links.quote: Token-level analysis localised instability to mid-chain stages (40–70% of the normalised trajectory); perplexity-based confidence failed to flag errors (AUROC 0·41–0·66).

design_hint: inference paradigms (back-translation pivot) and token-level uncertainty detection toolkit
